<reason>Both sides built coherent, well-structured cases, but A's mechanism—that credibility is inferred from outcomes and that any "conditional trigger" for tightening is inherently lagging—survived the exchange better than B's proportionality case. When A pressed for an observable threshold, B supplied one (two quarters of stalled disinflation plus rising expectations, with an "unmistakable deterioration" exception), but A's Rebuttal 2 showed this trigger only confirms entrenchment after wage contracts are already set, turning B's own answer into evidence for front-loaded action. B never directly rebutted this specific lag critique in its final speeches, instead re-asserting the existence of the exception without engaging the timing problem. A also successfully converted B's admission that demand suppression is the only real cure for embedded inflation into an argument that delay merely postpones and enlarges the same recession, which B's closing addressed only with a general burden-of-proof complaint ("calling it bigger doesn't establish it") rather than substantively countering the mechanism. B's strongest points—that the size of any recession is uncertain, that inflation's cost is not undone by acceleration, and that policy lags cut both ways—were real and forced A to sharpen its asymmetry argument, but they were answered rather than left standing. Both sides handled the Pressure Questions format correctly with A1/A2 labels, but A's questions extracted a more damaging concession (the lagging nature of B's own trigger) than B's questions did from A. The closings crystallized existing clash without major new evidence, but A's was tighter and directly hit the unresolved lag issue, while B's closing mischaracterized A's position as a fuller concession than it was.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A's Rebuttal 2 (A4.1–A4.2), showing that B's own proposed trigger (two quarters of stalled progress plus rising expectations) can only confirm entrenchment after wage contracts are already set—turning B's safeguard into evidence for A's "lagging indicator" critique, a point B's subsequent closing did not directly neutralize.</best_rebuttal>
